text: A baker in Pechersk just called. The bread’s in the oven and his customers are in the shelter across the street. He left me his number. He wants to know as soon as it’s safe for them to come out.
Our camera crew has found a hangar in Pechersk. We have yet to establish what’s inside. We can confirm that the word ‘biolab’ fits on the news ticker. Stay with us.
Five helicopters over Pechersk. It’ll be a while before the all-clear. Mr President, Bondarenko’s in position. Shall we open the hangar?
Open them. Until now, hardly anyone besides his keepers has seen that dragon. Today all of Kyiv will. Bondarenko, his keeper says a hand on his neck will steady him when he hears the engines.
Bondarenko, have your troops hold the doors so he doesn’t catch a wing. Once you’re airborne, the sky over Pechersk is yours to look after.
Both doors are wide open, but he’s dug his feet in. He’s looking right at me. Let me get this glove off. Coming, little fellow?
Give him a moment. Tell me what worked when you get back. I’ve checked our flight manuals, Bondarenko, and we haven’t got a single page on dragons yet.
I’ll keep the radio on. I’d like to hear from you myself when you land. Then I owe a baker a phone call. Glory to Ukraine!
